items.title: Completion along a closed subspace is compatible with base change

items.difficulty_reason: The statement is that for a morphism f : X' -> X of algebraic spaces over S and a closed subspace Z of X with inverse image Z', the square formed by the completions (X')^_{Z'}, X^_Z and the morphisms to X' and X is cartesian, and in particular the induced map (X')^_{Z'} -> X^_Z is representable by algebraic spaces (statement lines 8232-8246). The proof derives the cartesian square from the colimit presentation of both completions: a morphism Y -> X from a scheme that factors through Z is taken, the fibre product Y x_X X' is shown to factor through Z', the equality of the infinitesimal neighbourhoods Z'_n = X' x_X Z_n is recorded for all n, and the two colimit formulas X^_Z = colim Z_n and (X')^_{Z'} = colim Z'_n then give the claim (proof lines 8248-8257). The level is H2: the card is short, but the reader has to run the colimit presentation through a scheme-valued test object and observe that the infinitesimal neighbourhoods are pulled back exactly.
